story: Gary and Donna are at Gary's house on this hazy Tuesday afternoon, agreeing that he will join her pickleball session tomorrow, with Donna cheerfully insisting that everyone is terrible in their first week and promising iced tea and a spare paddle. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is dutifully counting the donna flamingo flock from the sidewalk for the record, while Rosa, optimistic as ever, invites him to dinner Saturday at six and tells him to bring only his appetite. Gary, warm and a little sheepish, is busy getting his cart lights sorted before the morning.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the record

gary.thought_process: Donna just offered to book a court for tomorrow morning, bring coffee, and let me finish the cart today. That's a fair deal, and honestly I've been looking forward to Saturday doubles, so I'll say yes without dragging it out. I'm not repeating my earlier pleading about being terrible. Short answer, thank her, then get back to the wiring. Also the speaker and permits are nagging at me, but that can wait until the cart is actually done.

parameters.content: That's a deal, Donna. Book it for tomorrow, I'll have the cart lights sorted by then, and I'll bring the sneakers. Save me a spot where I can do the least damage.

donna.thought_process: Gary just caved and said he needs two minutes to find his sneakers and unplug the soldering iron. I've already asked and he's already said yes, so pushing again would just be nagging. Better to settle the logistics: it's past 1 PM, so the court plan should be today if he's lacing up now. L-05 caps reservations at 2 hours, and I only need an hour or so. I'll keep it light, tell him there's no rush, and mention the spare paddle and coffee so he feels at ease about being terrible. Then we head out together.

parameters.content: Take your time, Gary, and don't you dare apologize for being terrible. Everybody's terrible for the first week, and I've got the spare paddle and a cooler of iced tea in the cart. Soldering iron off, sneakers on, and I'll drive.

hal.thought_process: Rosa pinned her dinner note, and I've already told her I'm coming and asked what time and what to bring. Asking again would be pestering. The bulletin board is right here, and I've been carrying a grievance about Donna's flamingo flock. The flock is visible from the street, which is exactly where L-02 draws the line. Before I go to dinner, I want a count on those birds so any report is accurate and not a hunch. By-the-book means facts first. If it's over three, it's a matter for the architectural review committee, and I'll sort out how to say it civilly before I sit at Rosa's table.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the record

rosa.thought_process: Hal said yes and asked two practical questions: what time and what to bring. I haven't given a time yet, so answering is the natural next step. Gary and Donna still need to be pinned down, but Hal's confirmation gets me one seat filled. I'll set a time that works around my per-diem shifts, tell him to bring nothing but himself, and keep it warm and a little teasing, since he promised to keep the rulebook in his pocket.

parameters.content: Glad you're coming, Hal. Saturday at six at my place. Bring nothing but yourself and an appetite, I've got the food covered, and the rulebook can stay in your pocket.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
